blocker: The nine repeated per-state bodies and the names/owner region. Structurally identical: same callees (0x2F9858 base ctor, 0x10A794 StateMgrBase, 0x14EB8C, 0x10BA78 x2, 0x10CEE0, 0x689800 x9, __aeabi_vec_ctor, 0x2AF5FC), same store offsets, same rodata table indices (1,2,3,4 for the hooks and 1..27 for the states), same loop shapes (2n-fill unrolled x2, n-fill with odd prologue, {0x24,n} cookie). What differs is armcc's register allocator inside each state block: the original hoists all six PMF words with one core register plus five VFP registers (`ldr r0,[sb,#0x28]; vldr s0,[sb,#0x30]; vldr s1,[sb,#8]; ...` then `str r0,[r1]; vstr s2,[r1,#4]`), mine keeps the six words in six VFP registers (`vldr s0..s5` then `vstr` pairs), which costs/merges one instruction per state (segments are 21-25 instructions on both sides, +/-1-3). That choice follows from the register pressure of the preceding block, which depends on the head (my head is 55 instructions vs 50 - the original keeps the zero constant in r5 and -1 in fp and only loads the PMF table base after the first hook store, mine loads the table base first and keeps 0 in fp). Fixing this needs the original source shape of the member-initialiser list; four orderings of the hook/scalar initialisers were tried and all produced the same 1636-byte body. Also tried and rejected: (a) all nine states through one helper that does the name copy plus the three handler stores (1376 bytes, 31.5%), (b) handlers-before-name order (1652 bytes, 46.5%), (c) one HookSet sub-object at +0x930 with an inline ctor - armcc refuses to inline it and emits a call instead (1556 bytes, 55.2% similarity but 9 instructions where the target has 50), (d) m980/m984 as two scalars, as a {20,-1} struct, and as an array; the array with the two stores at the top of the body is the one that matches best.
